[2021-11-01 02:45] mainecougar : For those interested in star ratings, this is the third season that I have been looking at them and have come to the conclusion that I haven’t figured out anything useful.  Long story, short, it appears that <@!711316787471581294> Dominican was right when he stated in a podcast that he thought star ratings could be based on a certain number of players being 5 stars, the next certain number 4 stars, etc. Read on if you would like the useless details I have learned.  As others have pointed out, star rating is determined using a player’s SI and potential.  As far as I am aware, the primary purpose of the star ratings is to replicate real life recruiting services that rank players by star rating in an effort to give a simplistic view of how talented they think a recruit is (and my personal opinion is that HW does a good job with this).  It is also my understanding that the only relevance to the game is language in the section of the Rules stating, “Additionally, teams with a history of red shirting highly rated players will also experience diminished recruiting prowess.” It is assumed that highly rated players mean 4 and 5 star players.   So I have been looking at this issue as I was curious to see if there was a certain SI level that the recruit had to attain in order to be considered a 4 star player or 5 star player (e.g., 12 pots need to hit 117 to be 4 stars and 135 to be 5 stars).  But that is not the case.
[2021-11-01 02:45] mainecougar : There are 3 star rating updates during the season, at development update #0 (during the flip), #5 and #10 (which was today).  Not sure why, but even though the SI shown for the beginning of each player’s freshman year in college (and every other season) includes SI gained during development update #0, the star rating for each freshman in college is determined based on development update #10.  At least that is what happened last season.  I kept track of the 4 and 5 stars at #10 last season and they all had the same star level as freshmen.  However, the SI needed for each level based on potential was a little off what I thought I had recorded during prior years.  I figured it was poor recordkeeping on my part as I didn’t realize the importance of that update.  But in looking at the numbers from today, the amount needed for each star level changes from year to year.  One other oddity, players on the border can be different star levels.  For example, this season the border between 3 and 4 stars for 12 pots is 115.  So everyone below 115 is a 3 star (or lower) and everyone above 115 is a 4 star (or 5 star if they get to 135).  But players at 115 can be either 4 star like-http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/118043 or can be 3 stars like http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/117931.  Last season, the border was 117.  Similarly, this season the border between 4 and 5 stars for 13 pots is 117/118.  Last season the border was 114/115.  So it fluctuates each season.   Last season there were 27 5 stars and 84 4 stars.  This year there are 28 5 stars and 80 4 stars.  So similar numbers.  Not sure why I ever doubted <@!711316787471581294> Dominican.

[2021-11-15 14:16] eljefe7705 : East      #5 Toledo Rockets (I.1) vs. #9 Washington State Cougars (IV.1) – a few injuries on Toledo make this interesting. They have the depth to accommodate, but the offensive becomes very one dimensional without Deliz. Wash U lacks size but has other metrics that play well on the interior to partially make up for it. They’re coming off a crazy comeback against IUPUI inspite of 28 TO’s, so not going to count them out here but I think Toledo is too good               #6 Wyoming Cowboys (IV.1) vs. #15 La Salle Explorers (IV.4) – Wyoming takes care of the ball and can score inside and out. LaSalle creates a ton of turnovers though, so something has to give. I think LaSalle’s run ends here due to the balanced scoring attack the Cowboys bring, and an expected inefficient game from David. Wyoming is looking like the Final Four rep from this region
[2021-11-15 14:17] eljefe7705 : Midwest     #5 Dominican Univ. of California Penguins (I.1) vs. #8 North Greenville Crusaders (I.1) – the rubber match between these two should be good. The Crusaders were an early season favorite in my book and after a rocky start, they have righted the ship. Similarly, Angel Reyes on the Penguins has turned his season around and made DUCA a lot more dangerous. This is a complete coin toss, but I’ll go with North Greenville             #11 Methodist University Monarchs (II.2) vs. #10 LSU Tigers (IV.5) – The Monarchs are going for their 2nd Sweet 16 in 3 seasons. The Lancaster brothers might have lived with different parents as children growing up in North Carolina, but the chemistry is there for a strong offensive attack. LSU is a damn fine team, and I think Tyler Lawrence will explode in this game with Edgar out for Methodist. LSU in a close one
[2021-11-15 14:17] eljefe7705 : South      #4 Tennessee Volunteers (I.1) vs. #9 Iowa Hawkeyes (I.1) – another Legends matchup as Iowa and Tennessee meet for the 4th time! I underestimated both teams this season so whoever I picked here probably loses. Pretty even up and down the lineup; Hyatt and Cunningham will get their points so winner will be who controls the interior. Iowa with the W               #6 Iona Gaels (II.1) vs. #10 Macalester Scots (IV.6) – Ollie Mann with an impressive showing as a FR, vs Wine13’s other team! Iona lights it up from downtown whereas the Scots play mostly opposite of FGCU and rely on a strong interior presence to pick up W’s. The Scots don’t have the outside shooting that typically plays well against Iona but they have a huge advantage on the interior which I think gets them the win here
[2021-11-15 14:17] eljefe7705 : West      #5 Huntington University Foresters (I.1) vs. #1 Alabama Crimson Tide (III.1) – Probably the best matchup of the Sweet 16 in my opinion. Alabama is another balanced team with talent everywhere and a great defense; definitely a National Title contender but a tough road to get there. Huntington has the talented bigs to combat…if not better Alabama’s and has the advantage at SF. The guards are where they will need to make up ground. Going to go with Alabama here               #3 Virginia Military Institute Keydets (III.2) vs. #7 Black Hills State Yellow Jackets (III.1) – Another III.1 team that beat me down this season. The Yellow Jackets are streaky but should have a huge advantage here against an undersized and overmatched VMI. The Keydets could absolutely get hot from 3-pt range, but that doesn’t seem to be the formula to beat Black Hills. Yellow Jackets with the win

[2021-11-26 03:22] kauffdaddyecsu : There are several facets behind sports/journalism jobs disappearing, but most boil down to two things: 1. Newspapers were profitable mainly because national companies paid significant amounts of money to advertise in them, and once the internet developed those advertisers no longer had any real need for newspapers, which dried most of the profits up. 2. The vast majority of newspapers/media are now owned by a small handful of very large companies (my paper got bought by Gannett two years ago), and they are all "streamlining" their business models because of the economic realities caused by No. 1. I believe within 10 years, almost all non-major city print newspapers will be extinct and many medium- and small-size towns will have no or very little news presence at all. The landscape will mostly be USA Today (under the Gannett umbrella), New York Times, Washington Post etc. That's a lot of reasonably good-paying paper jobs that will be poof, gone (and that trend started 15 years ago).

[2022-01-22 03:37] chaz_egan12 : new to the game, how do divisions work?
[2022-01-22 03:40] naph7777 : Conferences are a pyramid structure from I to VI (only 1 at level 1, 2 at level 2, 4 at level 3 etc). All the leagues from I to IV are division 1. League Level V (LL5) is division 2. LL6 is division 3.  LL5 teams have a penalty in raising interest on 5-star players. LL6 teams have a penalty in raising interest on 4 and 5-star players.  Each division plays its own separate tournament at the end of the season.
[2022-01-22 03:42] naph7777 : Teams move up and down conferences each season. Top 3 go up. Bottom 6 go down (3 to each of the two conferences below them)
[2022-01-22 03:43] naph7777 : Does that cover everything? Or is there something else you wanted to know about?

[2022-02-28 16:19] slickandjakenillinois : I don’t think head to head matchup has any weight.  The three main variables in the tournament seeding appear to be league level, place in the conference, and RPI.  It should be noted RPI is impacted by other measurements such as SOS and WP, so the other measurements may play minor roles in the seeding as well, but RPI likely encapsulates all other variables. So Marist’s 0.009 higher RPI is slightly more important than Marquette’s one higher place in the conference standings.  And Clark’s 0.005 higher RPI is slightly more important than Nazareth’s one higher place in the conference.

I always end up with some weird results that differ from reality because owners value their players and skills differently than I do and use them accordingly.  I'm always tempted to reach out to presidents and get their insights on their team, which would make the previews a lot more accurate. [2022-07-11 15:51] bradenwoa : The transfer portal for me has two core issues that have to be addressed, and any solution has to address both before it can be worthwhile to even discuss limitations and implementation.  1.  How do you make it fun, rather than frustrating for users?  Hardwood doesn’t have a robust communication system for interacting with players the way something like Football Manager does.  It’s really hard to have player driven transfers without it feeling too luck based or frustrating.  Even a morale system has the issue of being either something that has to be micromanaged, taking away some of the value of Hardwood as a game that can be played casually or in depth, or something that is finicky that ends up being a confusing/frustrating black box type (see: playing time penalties circa 2010).  The real life back and forth between player and coach isn’t really something that you can replicate in Hardwood, which must be accounted for. 2. How do you ensure good players end up in the transfer portal?  If you don’t have good players in the portal, it won’t provide much value and will be a waste of effort and resources.  In general, you don’t want to lose good players.  Compared to real life, stylistic fit is more important, and player development is more static and impactful.  This leads player valuation to be more consistent across the board.  There may be players that border on good, but rarely will you have players that one team will grade as “good” that another will grade as “useless”, which is really what the portal would be most useful for.  Any solution really needs to create a way to have good players in the pipeline, beyond beating up on bots, newbies, and second teams.  The reason I say it’s an inherently flawed idea is that these two core concerns are at odds.  Most ideas that address one will worsen the other. That doesn’t mean there isn’t some proposal that would work, it just creates a prerequisite to any discussion—the jumping off point must have some sort of answer to these two core issues.  Beyond that, a discussion can address the further concerns (limiting abuse, whether it’s a good idea to allow players to get out of bad decisions they’ve made, whether the transfer system is intuitive, whether it fits the current game well enough or would change the game too much, etc.).  For example, an idea I’ve thrown out privately is allowing owners to receive a portion of the contacts spent by other owners—this would solve the issue of being a frustrating system (you have the choice) and also incentivize adding good players to the system (you transfer players you think would be overvalued on the market, and get more back in recruiting points than the player is worth).  However, I haven’t been able to theorize that idea in such a way that it can’t be abused (funneling points), and wouldn’t radically change the game (basically adding a transfer market completely changes the economic landscape to the point that recruiting and team building systems are unrecognizable).  In short, any proposal really has to answer the two core issues, but then also has to pass other checks—this can potentially be done with refinement and discussion.
